guards.kind: node-only, pure logic. Imports engine/InteractionSessionMachine directly; the machine takes `now` as a parameter so every time-based case advances an explicit clock.
citedBy: none at entry — navigation.md names it in prose only, to say it is NOT a Navigation guard
guards.exitContractNote: Count-based and correct: exit 0 on failures.length === 0, exit 1 with each failing assertion named.
guards.break: Four breaks in engine/InteractionSessionMachine.ts, applied and reverted independently. (A) endInteraction's `count <= 0` guard removed, so an unbalanced end goes negative. (C) sourcePasses returns true for a non-matching `only` filter. (D) tickWatchdog ignores the activity refresh (`now >= max` instead of `now - lastActivity >= max`). (E) vanishing-input probe — renamed the exported isIdle so the guard's own import cannot resolve.
guards.result: ALL RED, distinct assertions. (A) exit 1, 3 failed: 'unbalanced end flagged', 'unbalanced end leaves session idle', 'no negative ref-count'. (C) exit 1, 2 failed: 'slider invisible to camera-filter', 'slider tail invisible to camera-filter'. (D) exit 1, 3 failed: 'recent poke keeps watchdog disarmed', 'still active after refresh', 'fires once poke goes stale'. (E) exit 1 — ESM link-time SyntaxError before any assertion runs.
guards.note: Fifth-failure-mode check: the corpus is inline in the guard itself, so it cannot vanish via a rename or a moved directory the way test:frag's external corpus did — and the one genuinely external input (the machine module) fails the guard at ESM link time, verified in (E). Residual: deleting a `test()` block lowers the printed assertion count silently, but that is a visible diff edit rather than a silent input loss, so no floor was added.

guards.note: The headline of the batch: a real, correctly-wired scrub producer — the dope-sheet key drag, whose own comment says it must read as `interacting` or the idle band renderer paints only the centre strip — could be completely de-wired from the InteractionSession and ALL THREE interaction guards stayed green at exit 0. Lesson 6 exactly, except the scope rather than the regex was one spelling away from blind. The tell was inside the gate's own source: utils/GraphDataSource.ts was listed as a SCRUB_PRODUCER while `utils` was not in SCAN_DIRS. Widening to hooks/utils/store (687 → 762 files) surfaced exactly two new scrub writers and zero new useDragValue importers, so the repair is low-noise; useDopeSheetInteraction is now a listed producer and useGraphInteraction a documented delegating exception (verified: its live-frame modes call ds.scrub?.begin(), and the one mode that sets isScrubbing without beginning, scrub_passive, deliberately skips ds.onAfterMutate so it never drives animationEngine.scrub). Sibling-app trees were deliberately NOT added and the reason is recorded in the header — they inherit the session from the connected wrappers in components/ and test:interaction:wiring asserts their inertness, so scanning them would flag legitimate consumers as uncovered producers. Process note worth keeping: the file floor was first set to 900 from a measurement of the WRONG directory set (1031), and the guard itself caught it on the next run.

guards.kind: node-only. Two halves: the worker read path through buildRenderInteractionState (the silent-key-typo guard), and sibling-app inertness plus a wired-not-dead pass over createInteractionSlice.
guards.break: Four breaks, applied and reverted independently. (K) deriveInteracting returns sessionInteracting || isPlaying, collapsing the ADR-0061 scope boundary. (L) buildRenderInteractionState emits the key `interactng` — the exact silent typo the module exists to prevent. (M) isInteracting() writes reactively to the store. (N) beginInteraction writes per source-add instead of per edge.
guards.result: ALL RED. (K) 1 failed: 'playback is NOT gesture activity (scope boundary)'. (L) 5 failed, including 'a typo key reads undefined — exactly the silent-false the SSOT prevents' — AND npm run typecheck went red independently with TS2561 naming the typo, confirming the module JSDoc's claim that the Pick<EngineRenderState> return type makes a rename fail typecheck. (M) 1 failed: 'NO store writes from reads/watchdog (slice provably inert without producers)'. (N) 3 failed: 'second source begin writes nothing', 'non-final end writes nothing', 'active→idle is one write'.
guards.note: Two independent layers hold the key contract — the guard's runtime round-trip and the Pick<> type pin — and (L) proved both fire. Noted but NOT changed: createInteractionSlice's `_session` is a MODULE-LEVEL singleton, so every makeSliceHarness() in a run shares one machine. The inertness case asserts getLastActivityTime() === -Infinity, which only holds because it runs before the wired-not-dead case begins a gesture. Correct today, order-dependent tomorrow. Recorded in the new rule's invariants rather than repaired: changing the harness is a rewrite of a healthy guard.

guards.kind: Playwright. Seeds a 2-keyframe track on julia.power, plays, asserts the frame advanced and the bound param moved. fluid-toy/main.tsx imports installModulation from engine/animation/modulationTick, so the entry does reach the governed code — verified by break (P).
guards.exitContractNote: Throw-based, main().catch → exit 1. Stops at the first failure, which is normal for this harness shape.
guards.break: (P) installModulation early-returns so the ANIMATE tick is never registered. (Q) the DDFS scalar binder in AnimationEngine.ts writes nothing. (R) the UNDERSCORE vec-axis match disabled. (S) the scalar binder multiplies its write by 100.
guards.result: (P) RED, 'playback did not advance frame (stuck at 0)' — and RED on anim-vec2 and anim-orbit too, confirming all three ride the same tick registration. (Q) RED, 'playback not applying track values to store (julia.power still 2)', while anim-vec2 stayed GREEN. (R) GREEN here and RED on anim-vec2 alone. guards.verdict: healthy on the plumbing; value assertion was loose (repaired)
guards.note: Lesson 5 measured rather than assumed: `!== 2` is satisfied by any wrong number, and its sibling smoke:anim-vec2 already range-checks the same shape. The range rather than an exact value because the sample instant is timing-dependent — observed currentFrame 22 (interpolated, 4.93) and 30.5 (clamped, 6) on the same unmodified tree — and a flaky assertion would be worse than a loose one. Residual limit recorded in source: a wrong value still inside [2, 6] passes. Also recorded: an earlier suspicion that the 700ms window always overshoots the last keyframe, so only the CLAMP branch is ever tested, turned out FALSE on measurement — runs land mid-interpolation about as often.

guards.kind: Playwright. Installs two quadrature Sine LFOs on julia.juliaC_x/_y and asserts liveModulations gains finite relative-add values.
guards.baselineNumbers: BEFORE exit 0, 7.2s. AFTER exit 0, ~8s; radii exactly 0.2000 on all six samples, spread 0.3826-0.4000 over five clean runs.
guards.break: Three breaks in engine/features/modulation/ModulationEngine.ts. (T) the Sine case forced to rawWave = 0 — a completely frozen LFO. (U) only the phase-0.25 partner killed — one dead axis. (W) the LFO phase never advances (time term zeroed).
guards.result: BEFORE REPAIR (T) was GREEN, exit 0, printing '✓ two-LFO orbit writes liveModulations (relative add)' with live juliaC identical to base to every decimal. AFTER REPAIR: (T) RED, radii all 0.0000. (U) RED on all three runs, radii scattered 0.0153-0.1973 as R|sin theta|. (W) RED on the SPREAD assertion alone with radii still exactly 0.2000 — clean isolation, and the case no single-sample check could ever see.
guards.verdict: cannot fail on a dead LFO (repaired)
guards.note: A guard whose entire subject is an ORBIT could not distinguish an orbit from a stationary point: every assertion was one-sided, and an offset of exactly zero is trivially within the radius. The repair leans on a property of the fixture rather than tolerance-tuning — the two LFOs are a quadrature pair, so hypot(dx, dy) = R independently of sample time, which is what makes a tight assertion possible in a smoke with nondeterministic timing; measured 0.2000 against RADIUS 0.2 on every sample of every clean run. Flake discipline (batch 4's smoke:liquify lesson): a 2-sample motion check was tried and REJECTED on measurement — separations of 0.3792 / 0.0777 / 0.3639 / 0.3583 over four clean runs left only 1.5x margin; the 6-sample spread gives ~4.8x.

guards.kind: Playwright. Seeds an UNDERSCORE-form track (julia.juliaC_x) and asserts the binder's vec-axis writer moved x, preserved y, and stayed in range.

guards.result: (P) RED, 'vec2 binder did not write x axis (still -0.7)'. (R) RED, same assertion, while smoke:anim-play and smoke:anim-orbit both stayed GREEN. (Q) GREEN, correctly: the underscore path does not go through the scalar setter.

guards.kind: Playwright. Mutates the Demo feature through the DDFS auto-setter and round-trips it through getPreset.
guards.baselineNumbers: BEFORE exit 0, 4.5s. AFTER exit 0, ~5s, three clean runs with no error-gate noise.

(AA) DemoOverlay throws on every render. (AB)/(AC) PresetLogic.sanitizeFeatureState only — colour forced to #000000, and y dropped from the vector branch.

AFTER REPAIR: (Y) RED 'vec2 param did not persist: position is {x:0,y:0}'; (Z) RED 'got r=0 g=1, expected r=1 g=0'; (AA) RED 'pageerror: DemoOverlay is dead'; (AB) RED 'save roundtrip lost color'; (AC) RED 'save roundtrip lost position: got {x:0.5,y:0}'.

guards.note: The smoke wrote color, position, size and opacity and checked only size and opacity — and its own comment documented the color gap as a decision. vec2 and color are exactly the two branches of the sanitiser most likely to break, because they CONSTRUCT a new object rather than passing the value through. The fixture is deliberately asymmetric (position.x 0.5, position.y -0.3) and (AC) proves it earns its keep — a single dropped axis is caught, which a symmetric fixture could not do (lesson 2). The page-error gate every sibling smoke already had was absent here; measured clean over three runs before adding it. The docstring's 'verifies the DemoOverlay reacts' is still only partly true — nothing can assert the overlay's pixels — but an overlay that cannot render at all is now a failure, and the comment says which of the two it is.

findings.summary: `_session` is a module-level singleton, so test-interaction-wiring.mts's three slice harnesses share one machine and its assertions are order-dependent — the inertness case's `getLastActivityTime() === -Infinity` holds only because it runs before the wired-not-dead case opens a gesture.
findings.rationale: Correct today and verified so. Not applied because the fix is a rewrite of a healthy guard (a resettable machine, or a factory instead of a module singleton), which this batch's brief forbids, and the singleton is deliberate — the JSDoc says it mirrors viewportSlice's `_adaptive` ref for hot-path reasons. Options: (a) leave it and rely on the caveat now recorded in .claude/rules/interaction-session.md's invariants, which is what was done; (b) export a test-only reset from the slice and call it in makeSliceHarness, which makes the tests order-independent at the cost of a test-shaped export on a hot-path module; (c) move the ref into a closure the slice factory owns, which is the clean fix but changes runtime behaviour for any app composing more than one store. Recommendation: (a) now, (b) if a fourth harness case is ever added — the risk is not the current tests failing, it is a future case being inserted above the inertness one and silently invalidating it.

findings.summary: The repaired range assertion still cannot catch a wrong value that lands inside [2, 6] — an inverted or rescaled interpolation that stays within the keyframe endpoints passes.
findings.rationale: Tightening it needs a deterministic sample point, and there isn't one: playback position at the 700ms mark varied from frame 22 to frame 49 across observed runs. Options: (a) leave the range and the recorded limitation, which is what was done; (b) pause playback at a known frame before sampling and assert the exact interpolated value, which is deterministic but changes what the smoke exercises (it would stop proving that free-running playback drives the param); (c) sample repeatedly and assert monotonicity, which catches inversion but adds ~1s and some flake surface. Recommendation: (b) as a SECOND assertion alongside the existing one rather than a replacement — seek to frame 15, assert julia.power === 4 exactly — but that is a design choice about what the smoke is for, hence Tier B.
